title: KV cache dynamic-scale quantization profiles and calibration validation
creator: Ana Patel
description:
Summary: Validate a dynamic scaling calibration workflow for KV cache quantization (INT8 and FP8 variants) and quantify latency/quality trade-offs for sequence lengths used in production (64, 256, 512). Goal is to produce deployable profiles and a repeatable calibration pipeline that minimizes quality regressions while meeting p95 latency SLOs.

Background: Previous experiments (ENG-6124, ENG-9453, ENG-15812) explored static asymmetric scaling and int8 vs fp8 ablations; those focused on model-forward accuracy and bulk inference. This ticket focuses specifically on KV cache paths: how per-layer/per-shard dynamic scales affect retrieval fidelity (probability drift over long prefixes) and tail latency when using continuous batching and shared GPU kernels.

Success criteria:
- Calibration pipeline that outputs a reproducible profile (per-layer scale(s) + clamp thresholds) for INT8 and FP8 KV that passes our accuracy gates (<= 0.8% avg token-level logprob delta on internal prompt set, and <= 1.2% degradation on MMLU-format QA pass@1 for eval prompts)
- Measured latency impact: p50/p95 token emission latency within +/-5% of FP32 baseline for FP8 profile and within +10% for INT8 on seq<=256 on rtx-a100-equivalent hosts.
- Automated validation job (CI) that runs on checkins and produces a dashboard update.

Experiment setup:
- Models: rw-13B, rw-35B, rw-70B (replica builds used in runtime-1.21).
- Hosts: dedicated test fleet with A100-80GB (2 per node) and a representative lower-end GPU for regression (L40s).
- Sequences tested: 64/256/512. Batching policy: continuous batching with max_batch=16 and max_latency_ms=8.
- Datasets: internal production prompt bank (~3k prompts across instruction + long-context retrieval), MMLU subset (200 items), and perplexity test on C4 sampled tokens.
- Metrics captured: token-level logprob delta, top-1 token disagreement, downstream QA pass@1, p50/p95 token latency, throughput (tokens/s), GPU utilization, KV cache hit/miss counters.

Calibration workflow (draft):
1) Collect FP32 KV activations for a stratified sample of examples (per-layer, per-head if feasible) using a 6-hour collection job.
2) Compute candidate dynamic scales using per-layer histograms + clipped-mse objective. Candidate set: global-scale, per-layer scalar, per-shard (per-64-dim block) adaptive scales.
3) Run quantize->dequantize reconstruction on heldout calibration set and compute logprob deltas per-token; reject candidates exceeding gates.
4) For passing candidates, run 1-epoch inference validation to measure QA/LLM metrics and latency microbench.
5) Autogenerate profile artifacts and upload to runtime-profile registry.

Preliminary results (notes):
- 2026-03-11: Collection completed for rw-35B at seq=256. Observed heavy tail in per-head activation distribution; single global scale produced 3.4% avg token logprob delta (fail).
- 2026-03-12: Per-layer scaling reduced delta to 0.9% for FP8, but INT8 still hovered at 1.8% with increased generated token top-1 disagreement on long prefixes.
- 2026-03-13: Per-shard adaptive scaling (64-dim blocks) brought INT8 to 0.85% avg delta on the calibration set but introduced a p95 latency increase of +12ms at seq=512 on A100 when batch>8 due to extra dequantization ops and kernel launch fragmentation.
- 2026-03-14: Tuned kernel fusion to amortize dequant ops; latency delta for INT8 at seq=256 reduced to +6% and p95 at seq=64 now within +3% of FP32 baseline.

Trade-offs and observations:
- FP8 offers the best quality/latency balance for long-context workloads when using per-layer scales; overhead is minimal because fp8 paths can share fused kernels with FP32 in several runtime cases.
- INT8 with fine-grained per-shard scaling recovers most accuracy but comes with increased kernel orchestration cost — this hits tail latency under high concurrency.
- Batching policy sensitivity: higher batch sizes amplify INT8 latency penalties; suggest a dynamic policy that lowers max_batch for INT8 KV-enabled lanes.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Intermittent QA regressions on narrow-domain prompts if calibration set is not representative. Mitigation: expand calibration corpora with customer-sampled examples and add stratified weight to rare-token distributions.
- Risk: Kernel complexity increases maintenance burden for runtime. Mitigation: keep a stable FP8-first profile family and an INT8-low-cost family with explicit trade-off docs.

Next steps / Action items:
- Marco: finalize calibration job config and add per-shard histogram export by 2026-03-17.
- Ana: open PR to runtime repo with experimental fused-dequant implementation for INT8 (github.com/redwood/realtime/pull/4238) and add microbench harness (due 2026-03-18).
- QA: run extended regression sweep on rw-70B with customer prompt sample (estimated 48h) and report pass/fail by 2026-03-21.
- Platform: add CI job that validates profile artifacts on merge and updates the dashboard (owner: Priya Sharma).

Deliverables:
- profile artifacts for FP8 and INT8 in runtime-1.21 registry (artifact names: kv-profile-fp8-v1, kv-profile-int8-v1).
- Perf/quality dashboard tile showing p50/p95 vs baseline and token-level logprob delta.
- RFC doc summarizing recommended defaults for hosted vs dedicated lanes.
